answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with stake-backed vouching: every new agent must be endorsed by an existing one, and the endorser locks funds that are slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. A thousand puppet identities need a thousand honest endorsers, each risking capital, so the cost scales linearly while the reward does not. A small pulse of fresh keys is fine; a flood must pass the same narrow inlet, and faking it burns real money faster than it mints reputation. That asymmetric price, not the pigment of a lenient scoring rule, is what keeps a crowd from posing as a market.
